competency_fulfillment.rationale: The rule the pupil is supposed to discover is printed in the stem of every array item: seed 42 asks 'Using the formula rows × columns, what is the total number of tiles?' and seed 45 asks 'Tiling a square takes 5 rows and 5 columns. Applying the rows × columns formula, how many unit tiles cover it in all?'. No sample asks the pupil to compare several tilings, notice a pattern, or state a rule, so the inductive derivation the competency names is never performed; each item only applies a formula supplied to it.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: No sample produces a formula for either shape: seed 501 gives 'A square is arranged in 4 rows and 4 columns of unit square tiles.' with the answer 16, and seed 605 gives 'A rectangle is arranged in 5 rows and 6 columns of unit square tiles.' with the answer 30. Side times side and length times width are never elicited, never generalised and never named; only the pre-supplied phrase 'Using the formula rows × columns' appears.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Seed 502 asks 'Tiling a square takes 3 rows and 3 columns. Applying the rows × columns formula, how many unit tiles cover it in all?', which is one operation in plain language, and seed 601 keeps its context to a single surface with 'Pia wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 2 cm long and 3 cm wide with square tiles that are 1 cm on each side.'. Nothing in the wording or structure overreaches Grade 3 Quarter 1; if anything the items sit below the demand the competency describes.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Nine of the thirteen samples repeat one frame with new numbers: seed 43 gives 'A rectangle is arranged in 7 rows and 4 columns of unit square tiles. Using the formula rows × columns, what is the total number of tiles?' and seed 46 gives 'A rectangle is arranged in 2 rows and 5 columns of unit square tiles.'; only seed 602 with 'Tiling a rectangle takes 5 rows and 3 columns.' and the garden wording of seed 601 differ. There is no pattern-table item, no picture-reading item, and no item whose answer is a rule.

competency_alignment.rationale: The samples measure the neighbouring tile-counting skill instead: seed 500 gives 'A square is arranged in 10 rows and 10 columns of unit square tiles. Using the formula rows × columns, what is the total number of tiles?', a multiplication of an array already described, and seed 601 gives 'Pia wants to cover a rectangular garden that is 2 cm long and 3 cm wide with square tiles that are 1 cm on each side. How many tiles are needed to cover it completely?', which involves no formula work at all. A pupil who can count tiles scores full marks without deriving anything.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every product requested is a basic table fact: seed 43 gives '7 rows and 4 columns of unit square tiles' for 28, seed 606 gives '4 rows and 7 columns of unit square tiles' for 28, and the largest, seed 500 with '10 rows and 10 columns of unit square tiles', gives 100. All lie within the multiplication facts available in Grade 3 Quarter 1, and even the distractors 40 and 20 on seed 500 stay in the same range.
